::: {#exr-pipes}
#### Pipes between houses

Seven houses, named $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$, $t$, $u$ and $w$, share a water system.
A pipe joins the two houses in each of these six pairs:

$$
\set{p, q}, \set{q, r}, \set{q, s}, \set{s, t}, \set{t, u}, \set{t, w}.
$$

@fig-pipes draws them.
How many routes are there from house $r$ to house $w$ that go along pipes and visit no house twice?

::: {#fig-pipes}

![](../images/trees-pipes.png){fig-alt="Seven points joined by six lines.
On the left, p and r are each joined to q.
In the middle, q is joined to s, and s is joined to t.
On the right, t is joined to u and to w." width="60%"}
